rules.message: Database '{{node.id}}' is written by application servers and the design has a search index, but no change-data-capture propagates its updates. Index writes rely on dual writes.
Cache '{{node.id}}' is the primary store for its data but has persistence disabled.
Cache '{{node.id}}' has no eviction policy. Declare lru, lfu or ttl, or justify none explicitly.
Design '{{design.id}}' holds data but declares no credential rotation period and has no key-management node.
Synchronous edge '{{edge.from}}' -> '{{edge.to}}' crosses a cell boundary while the design requires cell isolation.
Datastore '{{node.id}}' has no backup or no retention policy declared.
Datastore '{{node.id}}' is single-region with no replication, but the design requires multi-region availability.
Search index '{{node.id}}' has no asynchronous feed from a stream, change data capture or worker. It cannot be rebuilt or kept in sync independently of the write path.

Edge '{{edge.from}}' -> '{{edge.to}}' claims exactly-once delivery, but '{{edge.to}}' calls a third party synchronously. Exactly-once cannot cover that side effect; make the external call idempotent instead.
Service '{{node.id}}' calls a third party inline with no queue or workflow engine to fall back to when that call fails.
Service '{{node.id}}' calls a worker synchronously. Hand the job to a queue or stream so the request path does not wait for fan-out.
Cache '{{node.id}}' holds materialised data but nothing durable or no worker feeds it. It cannot be rebuilt after loss.
Edge '{{edge.from}}' -> '{{edge.to}}' moves money but does not declare idempotent, while the design requires exactly-once effect. Add an idempotency key to this hop.
Design '{{design.id}}' requires zero-sum money movement but has no ledger node. Record money in an append-only double-entry ledger.
Store '{{node.id}}' is multi-leader across regions with no conflict resolution policy. Declare last-writer-wins, vector-clock or app-merge.
Object store '{{node.id}}' spans fewer than 3 zones (or declares none) while the design targets more than 10 nines of durability.
Topic '{{node.id}}' cannot replay messages, but the design requires replay. Use a stream or a replayable queue.
Worker '{{node.id}}' pushes fan-out over a social graph with no fanoutThreshold. Declare a follower threshold above which timelines are merged at read time.
Queue '{{node.id}}' receives async traffic but has no dead-letter queue.
Datastore '{{node.id}}' serves a read-heavy workload directly from application servers and the design has no cache.
Database '{{node.id}}' relies on async read replicas as its only scaling above 5000 rps. Replicas do not scale writes.
Realtime gateway '{{node.id}}' calls a coordination service synchronously on connect but has no reconnect stampede guard.
Retry queue '{{node.id}}' has no dead-letter queue. Messages that keep failing must be parked for manual investigation.
Edge '{{edge.from}}' -> '{{edge.to}}' retries without a circuit breaker, and '{{edge.to}}' has no rate limiter in front of it. Retry storms will cascade.
Retry queue '{{node.id}}' declares no backoff. Retries without backoff amplify the outage they are retrying through.
Shared dependency '{{node.id}}' is not redundant, but the design requires redundant discovery.
Realtime gateway '{{node.id}}' assigns channels randomly while the design declares heavy-tail traffic. Hot channels will degrade unrelated tenants on the same host.
Worker '{{node.id}}' consumes more than one queue while the design requires per-queue isolation. Give each queue its own worker pool.
Database '{{node.id}}' is a single unsharded writer declared at more than 5000 rps. Shard it or move to a multi-writer distributed store.
'{{node.id}}' is pinned to a single availability zone with no failover or replication.
Service '{{node.id}}' is on a consistent hash ring but is not connected to a coordination service that manages the ring.
Stateful node '{{node.id}}' lives in exactly one availability zone. A zone outage takes its state with it.
Realtime gateway '{{node.id}}' autoscales but does not drain connections on scale-in. Every scale-down becomes a reconnect storm.
Entry point '{{node.id}}' starts a synchronous call chain deeper than 3 hops while the design states a p95 latency target.
Webhook '{{node.id}}' does not verify signatures or is not idempotent. Verify the caller's signature and deduplicate by event id.
Stream processor '{{node.id}}' windows by event time but declares no watermark. Late data handling is undefined.

content-repository.name: Content repository

coordination-service.description: Strongly consistent service for metadata, locks, discovery and placement.
coordination-service.name: Coordination service

data-catalog.description: Scans data sources and holds their classifications, lineage and glossary.

data-warehouse.name: Data warehouse

database-proxy.description: Routing, pooling and shedding layer in front of a datastore.

ddos-protection.name: DDoS protection plan

email-security-gateway.description: Inspects inbound mail for phishing, malware and spoofing before it reaches the mailbox.
email-security-gateway.name: Email security gateway

event-store.description: Append-only replicated event log that is the system of record.
event-store.name: Event store

file-storage.description: A shared filesystem mounted by many machines over NFS or SMB.
file-storage.name: File share

firewall.description: A stateful packet filter that allows or denies traffic by rule.
firewall.name: Firewall

graph-database.description: Stores nodes and edges for adjacency queries.
graph-database.name: Graph database

iot-hub.description: A device gateway with a registry, per-device identity and twin state.
iot-hub.name: IoT hub

key-management.description: Holds keys and secrets and rotates them.
key-management.name: Key management

load-balancer.description: Spreads connections or requests across backends.
load-balancer.name: Load balancer

media-router.description: Routes live audio and video between participants or ingest and origins.
media-router.name: Media router

media-transcoder.description: Encodes audio and video into a rendition ladder for delivery.
media-transcoder.name: Media transcoder

ml-platform.description: A training workspace with compute targets, datasets and a model registry.
ml-platform.name: ML platform

monitoring.description: Collects metrics, logs or traces and raises alerts.
monitoring.name: Monitoring

nat-gateway.description: Outbound-only source address translation with a fixed egress address set.
nat-gateway.name: NAT gateway

network-fabric.description: Physical or overlay network the system depends on.
network-fabric.name: Network fabric

notification-service.description: Fans out messages to push, email and SMS channels.
notification-service.name: Notification service

policy-engine.description: Evaluates resources against governance rules and audits or blocks them.
policy-engine.name: Policy engine

private-link.description: A private network address that pins a managed service into a subnet.
private-link.name: Private endpoint

pubsub-topic.description: Fan-out topic. Every subscriber receives every message.
pubsub-topic.name: Pub/Sub topic

queue.description: Point-to-point message queue. Each message is processed by one consumer.
queue.name: Queue

rate-limiter.description: Bounds request or concurrency rate per key.
rate-limiter.name: Rate limiter

realtime-gateway.description: Holds long-lived client connections and pushes events.
realtime-gateway.name: Real-time gateway

search-index.description: Derived index for text, prefix, vector or geospatial queries.
search-index.name: Search index

service-mesh.description: Sidecar or library layer for service-to-service traffic.
service-mesh.name: Service mesh

sql-database.description: Relational datastore, usually the system of record.
sql-database.name: SQL database

stream.description: Partitioned, replayable, durable log read by offset.
stream.name: Stream

stream-processor.description: Continuous computation over streams with windows and state.
stream-processor.name: Stream processor

third-party-api.description: A service outside your control that you call.
third-party-api.name: Third-party API

timeseries-database.description: Metrics store with downsampling and tiered retention.
timeseries-database.name: Time-series database

vector-database.description: Stores embeddings and answers nearest-neighbour queries over them.
vector-database.name: Vector database

virtual-desktop.description: A brokered pool of session hosts serving remote desktops to users.
virtual-desktop.name: Virtual desktop pool

virtual-machine.description: A leased guest machine running an OS image on provider infrastructure.
virtual-machine.name: Virtual machine

vpn-gateway.description: An encrypted tunnel endpoint joining a network to a remote peer.
vpn-gateway.name: VPN gateway

waf.description: A layer-7 rule engine that inspects and blocks HTTP requests.
waf.name: Web application firewall

webhook-endpoint.description: HTTP endpoint that receives callbacks from a third party.
webhook-endpoint.name: Webhook endpoint

worker.description: Background process triggered by a queue, schedule, stream or batch.
worker.name: Worker

workflow-engine.description: Durable orchestration of multi-step processes with retries and compensation.
workflow-engine.name: Workflow engine

business-updates-without-index-propagati.description: Application servers write a database and the design keeps a search index, but no change data capture leaves the database; index writes rely on dual writes.
business-updates-without-index-propagati.name: Database updates not propagated to the search index

cache-as-primary-store-without-persisten.description: A cache is the only copy of its data and has persistence disabled, so the data is lost on restart.
cache-as-primary-store-without-persisten.name: Cache used as primary store without persistence

credentials-without-rotation.description: The design holds data but declares no credential rotation period and has no key-management node.
credentials-without-rotation.name: Credentials without rotation

cross-cell-call.description: A synchronous edge crosses a cell boundary while the design requires cell isolation.
cross-cell-call.name: Synchronous call across cells

datastore-single-region.name: Single-region datastore behind a multi-region SLA

derived-store-without-cdc-or-rebuild.description: A search index has no asynchronous in-edge from a stream, change data capture or worker, so it cannot be rebuilt or kept in sync off the write path.
derived-store-without-cdc-or-rebuild.name: Search index without an asynchronous feed

exactly-once-with-external-side-effects.description: An edge claims exactly-once delivery to a node that then calls a third party synchronously, which exactly-once cannot cover.
exactly-once-with-external-side-effects.name: Exactly-once delivery in front of an external side effect

external-call-inline-without-durable-pat.description: A service calls a third party synchronously and has no queue or workflow engine to hand the request to on failure.
external-call-inline-without-durable-pat.name: Inline external call without durable fallback

fanout-inline-in-request-path.description: An application server calls a worker synchronously, so the request waits for background work such as fan-out.
fanout-inline-in-request-path.name: Fan-out inline in the request path

materialised-cache-without-rebuild-path.description: A cache holds materialised data but has no in-edge from a durable store, worker or stream that could rebuild it.
materialised-cache-without-rebuild-path.name: Materialised cache without a rebuild path

money-mutation-without-idempotency-key.description: An edge into a money-handling third party or a double-entry ledger declares no idempotency while the design requires exactly-once effect.
money-mutation-without-idempotency-key.name: Money mutation without idempotency key

money-store-without-double-entry-ledger.description: The design requires zero-sum money movement but contains no ledger node.
money-store-without-double-entry-ledger.name: Money store without double-entry ledger

multi-leader-store-without-conflict-poli.description: A NoSQL store replicates multi-region multi-leader but declares no conflict resolution policy.
multi-leader-store-without-conflict-poli.name: Multi-leader store without a conflict policy

object-store-single-zone-with-durability.description: An object store spans fewer than three zones, or declares none, while the design targets more than ten nines of annual durability.
object-store-single-zone-with-durability.name: Object store in fewer than three zones with a durability target

pubsub-replay-required.name: Pub/Sub topic where replay is required

push-fanout-without-celebrity-path.description: A worker pushes fan-out over a social graph with no follower threshold above which timelines are merged at read time.
push-fanout-without-celebrity-path.name: Push fan-out without a celebrity threshold

read-heavy-path-without-cache.description: The design states a read-heavy workload and application servers read a datastore directly, but no cache exists.
read-heavy-path-without-cache.name: Read-heavy datastore without a cache

read-replica-as-sole-scaling.description: An SQL database above 5000 rps relies on async replicas alone; it is neither sharded nor distributed, so writes still hit one primary.
read-replica-as-sole-scaling.name: Read replicas as the only scaling

reconnect-stampede-without-guard.description: A realtime gateway calls a coordination service synchronously on connect and has no guard against a mass reconnect.
reconnect-stampede-without-guard.name: Reconnect stampede without guard

retry-queue-without-dlq.description: A queue in the retry role has no dead-letter queue, so poison messages are retried forever or dropped.
retry-queue-without-dlq.name: Retry queue without dead-letter queue

retry-without-adaptive-shedding.description: An edge retries into a service with no circuit breaker on the caller and no rate limiter in front of the callee.
retry-without-adaptive-shedding.name: Retry without circuit breaker or load shedding

retry-without-backoff.description: A queue in the retry role declares no backoff, so retries hammer the failing dependency.
retry-without-backoff.name: Retry queue without backoff

shared-dependency-without-redundancy.description: The design requires redundant discovery, but a DNS or coordination service has a single provider or is not replicated.
shared-dependency-without-redundancy.name: Shared dependency without redundancy

shared-host-per-channel-without-isolatio.description: A realtime gateway assigns channels to hosts at random while the design declares heavy-tail traffic, so hot channels degrade unrelated tenants.
shared-host-per-channel-without-isolatio.name: Random channel placement under heavy-tail traffic

shared-worker-pool-across-queues.description: One worker consumes more than one queue while the design requires per-queue isolation.
shared-worker-pool-across-queues.name: Shared worker pool across queues

single-writer-primary-at-peak-qps.description: An unsharded single-writer SQL database is declared at more than 5000 requests per second.
single-writer-primary-at-peak-qps.name: Single-writer primary at peak QPS

stateful-engine-pinned-to-single-zone.description: A matching engine, coordination service or event store sits in exactly one availability zone with no failover or replication.
stateful-engine-pinned-to-single-zone.name: Stateful engine pinned to a single zone

stateful-hash-ring-without-ring-manager.description: A service on a consistent hash ring is not connected to a coordination service that owns the ring.
stateful-hash-ring-without-ring-manager.name: Stateful hash ring without ring manager

stateful-node-without-zone-redundancy.description: A stateful compute node lives in exactly one availability zone and is not part of a cell.
stateful-node-without-zone-redundancy.name: Stateful node without zone redundancy

stateful-websocket-scale-in-without-drai.description: An autoscaling realtime gateway does not drain connections when scaling in, so every scale-down is a reconnect storm.
stateful-websocket-scale-in-without-drai.name: Stateful WebSocket scale-in without drain

webhook-without-signature-or-idempotency.description: A webhook endpoint accepts callbacks without verifying the caller's signature or without deduplicating retried events.
webhook-without-signature-or-idempotency.name: Webhook without signature verification or idempotency

windowed-aggregation-without-watermark.description: A stream processor windows by event time but declares no watermark, so window completion and late data are undefined.
windowed-aggregation-without-watermark.name: Event-time windows without watermark
